mechanism_narrative: A persistent drop in WORKPLACES together with depressed TRANSIT keeps weekday footfall away from shopping streets, so RETAIL_REC stays lower over the next four weeks than over the prior four weeks.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC rises above the last-4-week mean for four consecutive weeks while WORKPLACES and TRANSIT remain below baseline.

mechanism_narrative: When RESIDENTIAL remains above baseline while TRANSIT stays well below baseline, people substitute local home-centered activity for discretionary shopping trips, pulling RETAIL_REC down within one week.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT stays below -25 points for a full week
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not decline in the week after TRANSIT is below -25 and RESIDENTIAL is above baseline.

mechanism_narrative: A rebound in PARKS activity signals weekend weather and leisure crowds, and that same leisure demand spills into retail trips, lifting RETAIL_REC over the next two weeks.
candidate_trigger: PARKS rises by at least 10 points week-on-week
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC fails to rise above the prior two-week average within two weeks after a 10-point weekly increase in PARKS.

mechanism_narrative: If GROCERY_PHARM stays near baseline and PARKS normalizes after a spike, discretionary out-of-home demand is not being diverted to essentials or leisure, so retail activity only edges higher, not enough to change the four-week average materially.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC jumps by more than 5 points above the last-4-week mean despite stable GROCERY_PHARM and a falling PARKS series.

mechanism_narrative: A renewed decline in TRANSIT below its recent range indicates commuting suppression from policy or risk responses, which reduces impulse shopping and keeps RETAIL_REC lower over the next four weeks.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT falls below -30 points after having been above -30 the prior week
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not fall relative to the prior four weeks after TRANSIT crosses from above -30 to below -30.

mechanism_narrative: When WORKPLACES and TRANSIT both improve together, commuting-linked shopping trips recover in the same direction, producing a higher RETAIL_REC within two weeks.
candidate_trigger: WORKPLACES and TRANSIT each rise for two consecutive weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC fails to increase within two weeks after simultaneous two-week gains in WORKPLACES and TRANSIT.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in GROCERY_PHARM reflects routine local errands that anchor nearby retail trips; if that series rises while WORKPLACES remains weak, RETAIL_REC should move up modestly over four weeks.
candidate_trigger: GROCERY_PHARM moves above -3 points and stays there for two weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC remains flat or declines over four weeks after GROCERY_PHARM holds above -3 for two weeks.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp PARKS surge without a matching TRANSIT recovery signals weather-driven leisure substitution rather than broader urban activation, and that pattern suppresses retail visitation over the next week.
candidate_trigger: PARKS rises above +10 while TRANSIT remains below -25
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC increases in the week after PARKS exceeds +10 while TRANSIT stays below -25.
